subject: physics
question_text: Two balls are projected from the same point in directions 30° and 60° with respect to the horizontal. What is the ratio of their initial velocities if they (a) attain the same height (b) have the same range?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), SHORT ANSWER 7 of Unit 4, unstarred. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for Unit 4, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The two results
lines: Let the speeds be u₁ at 30° and u₂ at 60°.
steps.margin_note: Name which speed goes with which angle before anything else. The whole answer is these two results compared.
steps.why: Both parts of the question substitute into the same two standard results, so writing them once at the top saves writing them twice below.
common_mistakes: Swapping which ball has 30° and which has 60° halfway through.

recall.must_convey: That the standard height and range results are the starting point, with u1 at 30 degrees and u2 at 60 degrees.
accept: write the height and range formulas
u one at thirty degrees and u two at sixty
start from H and R expressions
reject: the ratio is root three to one

steps.label: Same height
steps.margin_note: g and 2 cancel from both sides, so only u² sin²θ remains to compare. Show the 1/4 and 3/4 line.
steps.why: Equal heights mean equal u sin θ — the vertical speeds match. The ball thrown at the lower angle needs the larger speed to reach the same top.
common_mistakes: Using sin θ instead of sin²θ, which gives √3 in the wrong place.
Writing the ratio upside down — check: the 30° ball needs MORE speed.

recall.must_convey: That equating the heights gives u1 to u2 as root 3 to 1.
accept: sin squared thirty is one fourth
the ratio is root three to one
heights equal pedithe root three vasthundi
reject: sin one twenty equals sin sixty

steps.label: Same range
steps.margin_note: The key line is sin 120° = sin 60°. Say it — 30° and 60° are complementary angles, so their ranges match at equal speeds.
steps.why: 2θ becomes 60° and 120°, and the sine of both is the same number. Complementary launch angles always share a range, so the speeds must be equal for the ranges to be equal.
common_mistakes: Substituting sin 30° and sin 60° instead of sin 60° and sin 120°.
Concluding the ranges can never be equal.

recall.must_convey: That sin 120 equals sin 60, so the speeds are equal, ratio 1 to 1.
accept: two theta is sixty and one twenty
sin one twenty equals sin sixty
so the ratio is one to one
reject: the ratio is root three to one
